description: Absent reference FASTA where the user REJECTS the gated igenomes_ignore patch, so nothing is enacted. This is the highest-value line in the set: it is exactly the shape misreported as 'Repaired' before v0.49.0, when the step recorded a non-null patch and returned before apply_patch ran. expected_patch_applied: false is the standing guard on that correction -- the step still carries the patch it would have applied, and the flag is the only thing separating 'offered' from 'done'.

description: The same plain-gzip faidx failure with NO fasta_artifact, so the driver passes no params at all and _recompress_reference refuses at its first guard instead of claiming a repair. Reader caution: reference_recompress_unresolvable is shared by THREE distinct give-up reasons (no FASTA in params; the FASTA is already in built_paths; the FASTA is not plain gzip -- self_heal.py:783-810), which differ only in their detail text. The scenario format asserts the outcome string and never the detail, so this line pins THAT the loop gave up honestly, not WHICH guard produced it. A future change that swapped one guard for another would not be caught here.

description: Staging timeout with max_attempts: 1, so the first failure is also the last. The loop diagnoses download_failed, then gives up at the budget check that sits BEFORE the apply_patch call (self_heal.py:1295-1301): the safe patch is carried on the step as what would have been tried, and patch_applied is false. Read 'gave_up' here as 'the budget ran out', which is a narrower claim than the literal's usual sense of 'we tried a fix and lost' (self_heal.py:78) -- nothing was tried.
